title: 2.3 Classification of Physical Quantities
description: Classification of Physical Quantities concepts and applications. Hard level, 20 questions.

questions.question: A quantity changes when its direction changes even if its size stays the same. Which classification fits?
Which set contains only fundamental quantities with their correct SI units?
options: Length in meter, mass in kilogram and time in second for students
Length in centimeter, mass in gram and time in minute in the unit
Force in newton and work in joule in the textbook of this subject
Speed in meter per second and density in kilogram per cubic meter
questions.correctAnswer: Length in meter, mass in kilogram and time in second for students

questions.question: A student lists mass, time and energy as vectors. Which correction is needed?
Which derived unit is equivalent to kilogram per meter per second squared?
Which derived unit is equivalent to meter squared per second squared?
Which relationship correctly expresses density using base quantities?
A graph shows a quantity with both size and direction. Which set could it belong to?
options: Distance, speed and time in experiments
Mass, temperature and energy in physics
Area, volume and work now in this topic

questions.question: Which comparison of fundamental and derived quantities is accurate?
options: Derived quantities are combinations of fundamental quantities
Fundamental quantities are combinations of derived quantities
The two categories are identical for students in the textbook
Derived quantities have no units for students in the textbook
questions.correctAnswer: Derived quantities are combinations of fundamental quantities

questions.question: Which pair of units are both derived?
A student writes that pressure equals force times area. Which correction is accurate?
options: Pressure equals force divided by area
Pressure equals area divided by force
questions.correctAnswer: Pressure equals force divided by area

questions.question: Which quantity has the same unit as distance?
Which set groups only vector quantities used in motion?
options: Distance, speed and time in experiments
Mass, force and energy now for students
Area, volume and density in experiments

questions.question: Which statement about the symbol for amount of substance is accurate?
options: Its quantity symbol is n and its unit is mole
Its quantity symbol is n and its unit is newton
Its quantity symbol is I and its unit is mole
Its quantity symbol is T and its unit is kelvin
questions.correctAnswer: Its quantity symbol is n and its unit is mole

questions.question: A derived quantity is expressed as kilogram meter per second squared. Which physical quantity is it?
Which description matches work in the textbook table?
options: Force multiplied by displacement, measured in joules in class
Force divided by area, measured in pascals now in experiments
Mass divided by volume, measured in kilograms per cubic meter
Distance divided by time, measured in meters per second still
questions.correctAnswer: Force multiplied by displacement, measured in joules in class

questions.question: Which description matches pressure in the textbook table?
options: Force divided by area, measured in pascals
Force multiplied by displacement, measured in joules
Mass divided by time, measured in kilograms per second
Area divided by volume, measured in per meter
questions.correctAnswer: Force divided by area, measured in pascals

questions.question: A quantity is described by a number and a unit only. Which classification applies?
Which example shows a vector being represented correctly?
options: Writing a displacement with an arrow over its symbol
Writing mass with an arrow over its symbol in nature
Writing time with an arrow over its symbol in nature
Writing temperature as a bold number in the textbook
questions.correctAnswer: Writing a displacement with an arrow over its symbol

questions.question: Which quantity is derived from two fundamental quantities but has no direction?
Which pair of quantities differ only in whether direction is included?
